subject.title: Support session-level environment variables for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-spawn ACP session env, and what credential boundary should that API enforce?
rationale: The requested surface can carry credentials and process-control values into host ACP subprocesses, so automation cannot safely choose between raw env injection, SecretRef-style indirection, trusted-caller gating, or deferring to per-agent env.

options.title: Add restricted session env
options.body: Expose session-level ACP env only through a validated and redacted contract that defines allowed sources, blocked keys, SecretRef handling, and persistent-session reuse behavior.

options.title: Prefer configured per-agent env
options.body: Close or defer this per-call API in favor of the safer configured `agents.list[].env` direction tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96229 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93425.

options.title: Reject tool-callable env
options.body: Keep ACP subprocess environment controlled only by host configuration and existing auth mechanisms to avoid model-controlled credential or process mutation.

recommendation.title: Add restricted session env
recommendation.body: Expose session-level ACP env only through a validated and redacted contract that defines allowed sources, blocked keys, SecretRef handling, and persistent-session reuse behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the ACP spawn/session API boundary introduced in the ACP thread-bound agents work.
